21.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria
21.work: Commentary on the Gospel of John, Book 11
21.text: Cyril makes 'that they all may be one, as Thou Father art in Me and I in Thee' the patristic charter of Christian unity. The pattern of the Church's oneness is the unity of the Father and the Son: not a unity of opinion, not a federation of like-minded persons, but a unity of nature shared. Christians are made one with each other by being made one with Christ, who is one with the Father. Whatever Christian unity is, it is grounded here, in the Trinity, or it is not unity at all.

21.author: St. Maximus the Confessor
21.text: Maximus reads John 17 as the foundation of theosis. Christ prays that those given to Him may be where He is, and may share in the glory given to Him by the Father. To be one with Christ as Christ is one with the Father is the destiny of the human person: not absorption into God, which would erase us, but communion with God, which makes us most fully ourselves. The Incarnation was not a temporary descent; it opened a way into the divine life that remains open through the Church and the sacraments.
